focus: Create a minimal gravity simulator as an audit-first deterministic small-N reference kernel, with close-encounter trust reporting as the main differentiator.
promoted_bridges: software verification -> audit-first deterministic reference kernel
software verification -> round-trip error as runtime trust signal
retired_bridges: large-N acceleration -> neighbor trees, event-sparse far field, and patch streaming
education/product packaging -> classroom or web sandbox framing
exact reversibility -> JANUS-style bitwise replay claims
next_experiments: Add star-grazing, unequal-mass flyby, and simple chaotic scenes to the benchmark suite and compare the direct kernel, encounter microstep branch, and REBOUND.
Test whether round-trip error predicts failure earlier than energy drift alone and export the trust metric in machine-readable reports.
Prove deterministic encounter-queue ordering across repeated runs and cross-runtime replays.
Evaluate offline-calibrated presets on held-out scenes and retire the preset branch if the ranking is unstable or hides softening sensitivity.
Keep evaluation centered on analytic two-body controls, conservation logs, timestep-halving convergence, and bounded replay envelopes.
